A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FOCoOp and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-E. Their corresponding content supports a reliable full comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, OOD detection, and generalization experiments, including module ablations, sensitivity studies, and additional results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains original FOCoOp and baseline experiments in the main text and Appendix E, including numerical results, ablations, and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The written server-selection procedure receives limited corrections: Equation (11) adds the minus sign for bottom-U selection, and Algorithm 3 removes eta-percentile instructions. These reconcile the specification with v1's existing selection description; they do not establish a changed implementation. The three-prompt design, BOS/GOC components, and main training objectives remain.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same classification, covariate-shift generalization, semantic OOD detection, and domain-generalization coverage. The evaluated datasets and test scenarios in Section 4 and Appendix E are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines: PromptFL, FedOTP, FedPGP, PromptFolio, FedLoCoOp, FedGalLoP, and FedLAPT. The smaller comparator subset in the ResNet50 experiment, Table 5, also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported client participation, communication rounds, local epochs, heterogeneity settings, backbone comparisons, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Both versions use the same leave-one-domain-out protocol and experimental settings in Section 4.1 and Appendix D.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical BOS/GOC ablations, shot and hyperparameter sensitivity studies, ResNet50 comparisons, and the prompt-similarity heatmap. No robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix D both report averages from three random seeds. There is no change to repeated-run disclosures, uncertainty reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Numerical results and empirical plots match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains FOCoOp's 93.85 ACC and 19.50 FPR95 for CIFAR-100 with 10 clients under pathological non-overlap. No result entries or empirical findings are added or revised.

T1.justification: The proof of Theorem C.3 removes an erroneous extra -log applied to the already defined loss in Equations (16)-(18) and associated derivation text. This repairs mathematical consistency with Equations (5)-(6). The underlying theorem conclusions, assumptions, and proof strategy are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about federated OOD-aware prompt learning, BOS/GOC, and improving robustness while maintaining generalization. No contribution or central claim is added, removed, or substantively strengthened.

C2.justification: The explanations of class/distribution separation, cross-client OOD ambiguity, and the roles of BOS and GOC remain substantively unchanged. The experimental interpretations introduce no new mechanism explanation, applicability boundary, or limitation.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures and the GitHub project link are unchanged. Both versions specify the same prompt initialization, length 16, embedding size 512, 100 OOD prompts, and training settings; no new hardware, runtime, or access information appears.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix A are unchanged. Describing the centralized comparator group as OOD robustness rather than OOD detection is a terminology refinement consistent with its existing discussion.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, clarifies class-indexed prompt notation, repairs the garbled explanation following Equation (7), and adds proof pointers. The section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes the schematic similarity ordering from s1 < s2 < s3 to S1 > S2 > S3 and replaces SemiUOT with SUOT. A few captions and dataset labels are standardized, with minor text reflow. The figure/table inventory and empirical displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves internal consistency through the selection-sign correction in Equation (11), removal of redundant negative logarithms in Appendix C, and corrected similarity ordering in Figure 2. These targeted repairs improve clarity and mathematical documentation. A new misleading reference to Table 5 as an appendix table is a small drawback, but the net benefit is positive and limited; empirical support and central claims remain unchanged.
